parole.testo: From Kipchak; ultimately from Proto-Turkic *bïčgak. Compare Romanian briceag and Albanian biçak. The form bicskia (“shomaker's knife”) is borrowed from Ottoman Turkish via Serbo-Croatian bičkija.

parole.significato: janissary (soldier in an elite Turkish guard)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish یڭیچری (yeñiçeri, “new troops”), perhaps via Serbo-Croatian janjičar.
